Definition: from G575 and G2476; to remove, i.e. (actively) instigate to revolt; usually (reflexively) to desist, desert, etc.:--depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self.
BiblicalUsage: To depart, to fall away — the devil departing from Jesus until a more convenient season, Gamaliel's counsel to refrain from these men and let them alone, the warning that some shall depart from the faith, and the call to take heed lest there be an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God. The word can describe a devil leaving, a council standing back, or a soul walking out on God.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that departing from the living God is the one departure this word warns me about above all others. The devil left Jesus and came back; those who leave the faith in the last days may not. I believe the guard is the one Hebrews names: take heed, and hold fast.
